sections.h2: Where is Texarkana, Arkansas, and why is it a twin city?
sections.html:
Texarkana, Arkansas is the county seat of Miller County, in the southwest corner of the state, and it shares a state line with its twin city, Texarkana, Texas. It is 143 miles southwest of Little Rock, 72 miles north of Shreveport, Louisiana, and 180 miles northeast of Dallas.

The city covers about 42.2 square miles of flat Gulf Coastal Plain in the Piney Woods, an oak-hickory forest region. Together the two cities anchor a metro area of 147,174 residents as of 2021. The Federal Courthouse, which also houses the city's only post office, sits directly on the Arkansas-Texas line and is the only federal office building that straddles a state line.

For a seller the border has one plain consequence. A Texarkana mailing address does not tell you which state a parcel is in, and the state decides which tax, title and probate rules apply. This page covers the Arkansas side.

Town lots were sold at a railroad intersection on December 8, 1873, a date both cities generally recognize as their founding, and Texarkana, Texas was founded the next year. Miller County has an older and stranger history than the city. It was formed in 1820 in the Arkansas Territory, named for James Miller, the territory's first governor, and dissolved in 1838 with its land given to Lafayette County. The Arkansas legislature re-established it in 1874.

Arkansas incorporated the city in 1880, though the sources we read give two different dates in August and October. Population grew from 1,390 in 1880 to 29,919 in 2010 and slipped to 29,387 in 2020. The Census Bureau estimates 29,123 for July 1, 2025. A city with a flat or slightly falling population and older housing stock is one where many sales involve heirs and absentee owners.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Texarkana housing?
sections.html:
Texarkana's housing costs are lower than the Arkansas metro areas to the north and east of it, and household incomes are lower too. These are Census Bureau QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024.

MeasureTexarkana, AR
Owner-occupied housing rate54.7%
Median value, owner-occupied homes$170,200
Median gross rent$909
Households11,333
Persons per household2.46
Median household income$45,835
Persons in poverty25.8%
Mean travel time to work17.1 minutes

One in four residents lives below the poverty line, and that shapes who sells in a hurry. Owners who fall behind on a mortgage, face a repair bill they cannot cover, or inherit a house with taxes owing often have limited cash and little time.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers around Texarkana?
sections.html:
The largest single employer near Texarkana is the Red River Army Depot, which employs more than 3,500 people. The 2018 employer report lists these Texarkana-area employers:

  • Red River Army Depot, 4,135 workers
  • Christus St. Michael Health Care, 1,800
  • Cooper Tire and Rubber, 1,750
  • AECOM/URS, 1,300

The depot is about 18 miles west of the city in Bowie County, Texas. It was activated in 1941 as an ammunition storage site and now rebuilds Army vehicles and rocket systems on 15,375 acres. The Base Realignment and Closure Commission recommended closing it in 1995 and again in 2005, and it stayed open both times. When a federal installation is on a recommended closure list, local owners feel it, and some sell early. Check current news about the depot if you are timing a sale.

The city's economy began as a rail trading center and still rests on agriculture and trade. Miller County also has a strong industrial manufacturing base.

sections.h2: What roads and airport does Texarkana have?
sections.html:
Three interstates meet at Texarkana: I-30, I-49 and the future I-69. That makes it a freight and travel crossing between Little Rock, Dallas and Shreveport. The commute figure above, 17.1 minutes, is short.

Texarkana Regional Airport is three miles northeast of the city on 964 acres. It is a mixed-use field with mainly general aviation and limited commercial service. A new terminal opened on June 28, 2024, named for E-Z Mart founder Jim E. Yates. It has two asphalt runways, 6,601 and 5,200 feet.

The Texarkana Arkansas School District is the largest public district on the Arkansas side, and it feeds Arkansas High School. A very small part of the city lies in the Genoa Central School District. The University of Arkansas Hope-Texarkana opened as a branch campus in 2012, Texarkana College is on the Texas side, and Trinity Christian School is a private Baptist school for pre-K through grade 12.

If your house is near the city's edge, verify the school district on your parcel before you advertise it. The Genoa line is the one that sometimes surprises owners.

sections.h2: What weather and drainage issues affect Texarkana houses?
sections.html: Texarkana has hot, humid summers, mild to cool winters, and about 48.9 inches of rain a year. Nix Creek is the main drainage, flowing into the Red River watershed. Flat ground and clay-rich coastal plain soil mean rain can sit on a lot, so inspectors look at grading, crawl spaces and gutters first. A seller who knows where water collects on the property can answer that question honestly and avoid a late price cut.

sections.h2: Which city and county offices handle a Texarkana sale?
sections.html:
The city's Planning and Zoning Division sits within Public Works at 216 Walnut Street, and it reviews building permits, special use requests and zoning compliance. Call 870-779-4974 for Public Works or 870-779-4944 for the city planner. The Planning Commission, Historic District Commission and Board of Adjustment all meet under the city, and agendas are posted on the city's meeting portal. Texarkana uses a council-manager system.

The county offices are all at 400 Laurel Street, Texarkana, AR 71854:

  • Assessor, Suite 100, 870-774-1502
  • Collector, Suite 111, 870-774-1001
  • Treasurer, Suite 104, 870-774-0003
  • Circuit Clerk, Suite 109, 870-774-4501

Taxes in Arkansas are due October 15 each year. According to the Texarkana Gazette, real estate taxes that go unpaid can be certified to the Commissioner of State Lands, and the collector's office handles redemption questions at the number above. The Arkansas transfer tax on a deed is $3.30 per $1,000, so $330 on a $100,000 sale.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Texarkana?
sections.html: A cash sale suits owners who need a fixed closing date, who hold a house that would not pass a lender's appraisal, or who are settling an estate from out of town. A traditional listing may bring more on a well-kept house, so compare both. Cash Home Buyers buys houses as-is in Arkansas and writes an offer after learning the facts of the property.

faqs.q: Is Texarkana, Arkansas the same as Texarkana, Texas?
faqs.a: No. They are twin cities on opposite sides of the state line, with separate city governments and different state laws. The Arkansas side is the county seat of Miller County.

faqs.q: How many people live in Texarkana, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 29,123 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 29,387.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Texarkana, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $170,200 for owner-occupied homes from 2020 to 2024. It is a survey median, and a single house can sit well above or below it.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Miller County?
faqs.a: The Miller County Collector, Suite 111 at 400 Laurel Street, phone 870-774-1001. Arkansas real estate and personal property taxes are due October 15.

faqs.q: Which office handles building permits in Texarkana, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The city's Planning and Zoning Division within Public Works, at 216 Walnut Street. The Public Works number is 870-779-4974.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Texarkana house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers commonly purchase as-is, so you do not have to fix the roof, foundation or drainage before closing.
